A Balanced Attack

They're a heavy under-center team (48% shotgun vs ~68%) — a pro-style, run-committed structure.

The Offensive Blueprint

In the passing game the ball funnels to their WR1 — 29% of targets (league ~23%), a genuine alpha share that concentrates the receiving value at the top.

Their backs are a real part of the passing game — RBs see 22% of targets (vs ~18%), which props up the back's reception floor.

It's a short, rhythm-based passing game — aDOT just 6.5 — that lives on YAC and checkdowns, boosting reception totals over big-play yardage.

When they fall behind they abandon the run entirely — 59% pass while trailing, so their pass-catchers have huge comeback-script ceilings.

By the numbers it's an efficient unit — a 48% success rate (above the 44% average).

In the Red Zone

Their red-zone identity is run-first (50% pass), funnelling touchdown equity to the lead back.

Defense — No Obvious Seam

Soft against opposing WR2s — 45 rec yds/game (vs ~36). A rec-yards target.

They give up deep shots (24% of throws travel 15+ vs ~19%) — big-play WR upside against them.

They surrender 109 rushing and 249 passing yards per game (league ~120 / ~230). No dominant funnel — read it matchup by matchup.

They leak RB rushing TDs (0.63/game vs ~0.46) — an anytime-TD spot to attack.

They leak TE touchdowns (0.29/game vs ~0.24) — an anytime-TD spot to attack.

The Betting Angles

Bottom line: their pass-catchers have massive ceilings in comeback scripts (fade-material as underdogs); opposing TE anytime-TD is a repeatable angle.

Built on 2024–25 data; the profile rebuilds through the season as the current staff and roster set their own tendencies.
